도서관.x: I borrowed a book from the library.
도서관.e: Literally 'book building'. -관 = building, as in 영화관 (movie theater).

케이크.e: From English 'cake' — note the extra syllable: 'keikeu'.

말씀하시다.x: The teacher said there's a test tomorrow.
말씀하시다.e: 말씀 (polite word for 말, speech) + 하시다.

성적.x: My grades went up a lot this semester.
성적.t: Grades 오르다 (go up) or 떨어지다 (drop); 성적이 좋다/나쁘다 for good or bad.

님.x: Mr. Hong Gil-dong, please come into the exam room now.
님.e: Respect suffix also found in 선생님, 사장님 and 부모님.
님.t: More respectful than 씨; used by staff to customers and in online communities after usernames.

께.forms: Honorific of 에게/한테; used after a respected person: 선생님께
께.ex: 저는 어버이날에 어머니께 예쁜 꽃을 드렸어요.
께.x: On Parents' Day, I gave my mother pretty flowers.
께.t: Pair 께 with humble verbs: 주다 becomes 드리다, 말하다 becomes 말씀드리다.

영양.ex: 아플 때는 영양이 많은 음식을 먹어야 해요.
영양.x: When you're sick, you should eat nutritious food.

하반기.ex: 회사는 하반기에 직원을 더 뽑을 계획이에요.
하반기.x: The company plans to hire more employees in the second half of the year.
하반기.e: Literally 'lower half period' — July to December.
하반기.t: Common in business news and job ads, e.g. 하반기 공채 'second-half open recruitment'.

경제적.x: Using public transportation is more economical.
경제적.t: Can mean both 'economic' (경제적 문제) and 'money-saving' (경제적인 차).

순하다.ex: 우리 집 강아지는 성격이 아주 순해요.
순하다.x: Our dog has a very gentle personality.
순하다.t: Also for mild flavors or products: 순한 맛 = mild flavor, 순한 화장품 = gentle cosmetics.

사진관.x: I went to a photo studio to get my passport photo taken.
사진관.t: The place to get ID and passport photos (증명사진); most studios retouch them for you.

뭐랄까.m: how should I put it, sort of
뭐랄까.x: That movie was, how should I put it, kind of strange.
뭐랄까.e: Contraction of 뭐라고 할까 'what shall I call it'.
뭐랄까.t: Buys time while you look for the right word; common in casual talk and interviews.

최저 임금.x: This year's minimum wage went up from last year.

이민자.ex: 미국에는 여러 나라에서 온 이민자가 많아요.
이민자.x: There are many immigrants from various countries in America.

사기꾼.ex: 그 사기꾼은 노인들을 속여서 돈을 받았어요.
사기꾼.x: That con artist tricked elderly people and took their money.
사기꾼.e: 사기 'fraud' + -꾼 'person who does it', often negative, as in 장사꾼, 노름꾼.
사기꾼.t: 사기를 당하다 = to be scammed; 사기를 치다 = to scam someone.

은하수.ex: 시골에서는 밤하늘의 은하수를 볼 수 있어요.
은하수.x: In the countryside, you can see the Milky Way in the night sky.
은하수.t: In the folktale 견우와 직녀, the two lovers are separated by the 은하수.

소유권.x: Ownership of this building belongs to City Hall.

조만간.forms: 조만간 + future: 조만간 만나요, 조만간 ~ㄹ 거예요
조만간.m: soon, before long, sooner or later
조만간.x: Let's grab a meal together sometime soon.
조만간.e: Literally 'between early and late' — sooner or later.

이에 반해.forms: A. 이에 반해 B (formal); N에 반해
이에 반해.m: in contrast, on the other hand
이에 반해.ex: 도시는 인구가 늘고 있습니다. 이에 반해 농촌은 인구가 줄고 있습니다.
이에 반해.x: Cities are growing in population. In contrast, rural areas are shrinking.
이에 반해.e: Literally 'opposing this' — 이 'this' + 에 반하다 'to run contrary to'.
이에 반해.t: Common in TOPIK writing task 53 for comparing data.

이처럼.m: like this, in this way, as shown
이처럼.ex: 이처럼 운동은 건강에 많은 도움이 됩니다.
이처럼.x: As shown, exercise is very good for your health.

납득하다.m: to understand and accept, to be convinced
납득하다.ex: 그 설명은 도저히 납득할 수가 없어요.
납득하다.x: I just can't accept that explanation.
납득하다.t: Pronounced [납뜨카다]; often negative: 납득이 안 가요 'It doesn't make sense to me.'

굶주리다.m: to starve, to go hungry; to hunger for, to crave
굶주리다.ex: 전쟁 때문에 많은 아이들이 굶주리고 있습니다.
굶주리다.x: Many children are starving because of the war.
굶주리다.e: Built on 굶다 'to skip meals': this is the long-term, serious version.

맥락.x: The meaning of a word changes depending on the context.
맥락.e: Literally 'veins and links': how ideas connect like blood vessels.

양육.ex: 요즘은 아빠들도 아이 양육에 많이 참여해요.
양육.x: These days, dads also take a big part in raising their kids.
양육.t: 육아 is the everyday word for childcare; 양육 is more formal and legal, as in 양육권 (custody).

잦아들다.forms: 잦아들어요 · 잦아들었어요 · 잦아들 거예요 · 잦아든 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
잦아들다.m: to die down, to subside, to fade away
잦아들다.ex: 밤이 되자 거센 바람이 조금씩 잦아들었어요.
잦아들다.x: When night came, the strong wind gradually died down.
잦아들다.e: From 잦다 'to dry up, ebb' plus 들다 — like water slowly receding.

스태그플레이션.ex: 전문가들은 스태그플레이션이 올 수도 있다고 경고했습니다.
스태그플레이션.x: Experts warned that stagflation could be coming.

결의안.x: The resolution was adopted overwhelmingly at the UN General Assembly.
결의안.t: Pronounced [겨리안]; common verbs: 결의안을 채택하다 (adopt) and 결의안을 통과시키다 (pass).

제노사이드.ex: 국제법은 제노사이드를 가장 심각한 범죄로 봅니다.
제노사이드.x: International law regards genocide as the most serious crime.
제노사이드.e: From English 'genocide'; the Korean equivalent is 집단학살 or 대량학살.

뇌출혈.x: My grandmother suddenly collapsed from a brain hemorrhage last month.
뇌출혈.e: Literally 'blood coming out in the brain'.

농악.x: Nongak was inscribed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2014.
농악.e: Literally 'farming music', played to cheer workers and pray for harvest.

조의금.ex: 흰 봉투에 조의금을 넣어서 접수대에 냈어요.
조의금.x: I put the condolence money in a white envelope and handed it in at the reception desk.
조의금.t: Odd amounts such as 30,000, 50,000 or 70,000 won are customary; 조의금 and 부의금 are used interchangeably.

판가름하다.m: to decide, to determine (an outcome), to settle
판가름하다.ex: 이번 경기가 우승 팀을 판가름할 거예요.
판가름하다.x: This game will decide the championship team.
판가름하다.e: From 판 'round, match' plus 가름 'dividing' — splitting winners from losers.
판가름하다.t: Intransitive 판가름이 나다 'to be settled' is just as common as the verb.

불가불.m: inevitably, unavoidably, having no choice but
불가불.ex: 사정이 생겨서 불가불 일정을 바꿔야 했어요.
불가불.x: Something came up, so I had no choice but to change the schedule.
불가불.e: Literally 'cannot not' — a double negative meaning 'must'.

명경지수.x: Meditation makes your mind clear as a bright mirror and still water.
명경지수.e: Literally 'bright mirror, still water': a mind without distractions.
